task: Build and execute CR005c Starbreaker escape-before-closure timing operationalization
objective: Determine whether the frozen Starbreaker three-stage carrier trajectories support an operational tau_escape < tau_closure ordering, using returned carrier-matter history 101 contacts and carrier-matter ending-zero histories without importing a physical timing law from the gravitational-wave branch.
source_use: Prior Starbreaker and gravitational-wave records are inputs and hypothesis context only; no predecessor verdict is retested.

primary_unit.anti_pseudoreplication: A carrier participating in multiple relations is counted once in primary timing statistics.
primary_unit.primary_population: carriers with at least one post-collapse ending-zero carrier-matter exit and at least one carrier-matter 101 return in the same scenario

stored_stage_parameter.interpolation: piecewise-linear relative position between stored stages

operational_dictionary.relation_surface: carrier-matter separation d equals the frozen Starbreaker contact radius r_contact = 0.076
operational_dictionary.release_surface: outward crossing of the relation surface; this is a local contact-release surface, not a horizon
operational_dictionary.escape_time: earliest outward crossing time among one carrier occurrence's ending-zero carrier-matter relations
operational_dictionary.postcollapse_escape_time: earliest outward crossing on collapse-to-final among history 010 or 110 carrier-matter relations
operational_dictionary.closure_time: earliest inward crossing on collapse-to-final among history 101 carrier-matter relations
operational_dictionary.scenario_closure_fronts: 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles of unique-carrier closure times within one scenario
operational_dictionary.history_100: seed contact exits before collapse and remains open
operational_dictionary.history_010: contact forms by collapse, exits before final, and remains open
operational_dictionary.history_110: seed/collapse contact exits before final and remains open
operational_dictionary.history_101: seed contact opens by collapse and returns before final

crossing_solver.root_domain: s in [0,1] on the one segment whose endpoint bits change

timing_ladder.strong: In both geometries and in discovery, validation, and final seed doors, more than 50 percent of dual post-collapse carrier occurrences satisfy tau_escape_post < tau_closure, and every cell has positive median closure-minus-escape margin.
timing_ladder.directional: Overall more than 50 percent satisfy the inequality, both geometry-level median margins are positive, and at least four of six frozen geometry-by-door cells have fraction above 0.50.
timing_ladder.boundary: The relation-time surface is constructed and source-reconciled, but the directional ordering is not stable enough for promotion.
timing_ladder.fail: A frozen source, roster, carrier-matter relation count, crossing root, or invariant control fails.

controls: all frozen source hashes match before and after execution
exact 18 carrier, 126 matter, 18 ledger-shadow typing per 162-slot ledger
carrier-matter history counts reconstructed exactly against the frozen relation-history aggregate
every transition crossing has one valid root and the expected normal-velocity sign
global translation and rigid rotation preserve crossing time
a synthetic affine crossing has its analytic time
half-radius and double-radius controls do not reproduce the frozen history census
wrong history-bit order does not reproduce the frozen asymmetric history census
no physical seconds, strain, distance, horizon, signal speed, fitted parameter, or SAM registry mutation is emitted

may_establish: an operational local relation surface native to frozen Starbreaker
dimensionless stored-stage escape and closure crossing times
whether ending-zero carrier contact release precedes 101 carrier contact return
the smallest source-side timing interface needed by a later gravitational-wave bridge
may_not_establish: a physical escape time or closure time in seconds
a global release surface, event horizon, or causal signal speed
gravitational-wave emission, strain, luminosity, or detector observables
